items.title: Muttil tree-felling case: Two accused surrender before Kerala court, get bail
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Two of the three Augustine brothers, key accused in the 2020 Muttil tree-felling case in Wayanad, surrendered before the Chottanikkara Judicial First Class Magistrate Court in Ernakulam on Tuesday, August 11, in a separate cheating case linked to the alleged sale of illegally felled timber. Jose Kutty Augustine and Anto Augustine, the second and third accused in the case, surrendered after the court issued non-bailable warrants against them for failing to appear. Their elder brother and the first accused, Roji Augustine, did not surrender before the court on Tuesday. According to reports, the magistrate court recalled the warrants against Jose Kutty and Anto after they appeared and granted them bail. The court directed all three accused to appear before it for the formal framing of charges. The three brothers are key accused in the 2020 Muttil tree-felling case, in which rosewood trees were allegedly cut down from assigned land in Wayanas. items.title: The questions posed by over 500 human remains found at Sri Lanka’s Chemmani mass grave
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A headless human skeleton with both hands bound and held against its chest was reportedly found at the Chemmani-Siththupathi mass grave in Jaffna, Sri Lanka, on Saturday, August 8. The discovery came as the excavation crossed 100 days, with 515 sets of human remains now identified at the site. The scale of the excavation has renewed attention on an allegation that dates back to Sri Lanka’s civil war: that hundreds of Tamil civilians who disappeared after the Sri Lankan military recaptured Jaffna in 1995, were killed and buried in the Chemmani area. The skeleton found last week was, as per a report in the Tamil Guardian, found lying in what appeared to be a normal resting position but without its skull. The neck had been severed, and both hands were bound and placed against the chest. Notably, this is not the first headless set of remains to be found at Chemmani. In earlier excavations, investigators also found remains where the head and body lie separated, including some in which the neck appeared to have been severed.
